newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money trades around 3.00 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money trades around 3.00 percent.

text.p: German call money rates kicked off the new week with slightly higher rates trading at around three percent compared with Friday's levels of 2.95/98 percent.

Traders said rich levels of commercial bank reserves held in non-interest bearing accounts at the Bundesbank seemed to indicate there would be no problem in meeting month-end reserve requirements. Dealers said rates, which can gyrate quite significantly at month-end, were not expected to exceed the 3.15 percent level in May.
The outlook for month-end however depends largely on this week's tender allocation from the central bank.
Dealers were expecting the Bundesbank would drain some funds this week as reserve holdings were ample, although at relatively low levels.
"The Bundesbank's preliminary minimum target of 39.5 billion marks represents a slight relief for the market," one trader said, after the figure came in at the lower end of expectations.
The Bundesbank said on Monday that banks held 41.8 billion marks in reserves as of Friday, up from 41.1 billion marks on Thursday, while the monthly average rose to 40.8 billion marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average on Monday was at 3.03267, compared with 3.04333 percent on Friday.
